sections.h2: Three things to finish before a Rockaway closing
sections.html:
The borough's sheet on selling a home names three items due before closing: a Certificate of Compliance for Fire Prevention, a final water reading, and property taxes paid in full. Each comes from a different office with its own fee, so start all three the day you have a contract.

This page covers Rockaway Borough, a Morris County municipality of 2.07 square miles. It had 6,598 residents in 2020 and an estimated 6,631 in July 2025. Rockaway Township borders the borough and runs its own separate offices, so check your tax bill to see which one holds your address before you phone anyone.

Zoning questions go to the borough zoning officer at Zoning@rockawayborough.org. The zoning office books appointments through 973-627-2000, extension 229.

The Bureau of Fire Prevention issues the certificate. Schedule by calling 973-625-3473 (973-625-FIRE) and leaving your name, address and phone number. Staff answer on weekdays and close at 4:30 p.m. The borough sheet, dated October 1, 2022, sets the fee by how early you ask.

Fire prevention certificate fees
When you request itFee
10 or more business days before closing$55 for the first inspection
4 to 10 business days before closing$90
Fewer than 4 business days before closing$200
Any later inspection$40

The sheet calls for a working smoke detector on each level including the basement, a carbon monoxide detector on each level that has bedrooms, no open building permits, and a house number at least 4 inches tall. It also lists a portable extinguisher, but state law removed that item from resale inspections in February 2025, so ask the bureau what it checks now. A house with a monitored fire alarm needs a test report dated within 12 months and someone on site who can reset the panel.

Call the Water Clerk at 973-627-2000, extension 223, for the final reading. The fee is $60 with 72 hours or more of notice and $95 with less, so ask early. Do not wait for the week of closing, since a short notice costs more and the clerk may not be able to fit the reading in.

A single-family house may set out three 32-gallon cans plus three bulk items each week. Condominiums and townhouses arrange their own collection of large items. If you are clearing out an inherited or vacant house, hire a hauler, because curbside service will not take everything.

The Construction Office, at 973-627-8035 on weekdays, handles the open permit check. Rockaway's property maintenance article requires a certificate of continued occupancy to sell or lease, but it covers nonresidential and mixed-occupancy buildings, so an ordinary house falls outside it.

Few households move in any given year here. In the 2020 to 2024 estimates, 97.1 percent of residents stayed at the same address over 12 months, against 87.7 percent nationally. The typical owner-occupied home is valued at $448,100 and owners hold 60.4 percent of the 2,711 households. Median household income is $107,053.

  • Typical owner-occupied home value: $448,100, against $332,700 nationally.
  • Monthly owner costs with a mortgage: $2,949, against $1,963.

Of 2,645 housing units counted in 2020, 3.2 percent were vacant, with a homeowner vacancy rate of 0.9 percent. Buyers have little to choose from, and a share of owners are older, so estate and downsizing sales make up part of what does come up. If your house is one of those, a clean file from the borough puts it ahead of a listing that still needs paperwork. The median age is 42.2, and 16.0 percent of residents are 65 or older.

sections.h2: Preparing the house for the fire visit
sections.html:
The inspection is quick when the house is ready for it. Walk through each level before the bureau arrives and check the smoke detectors, including the one in the basement, and the carbon monoxide detector on every level with bedrooms. Press each test button and replace any unit that stays silent.

Look at the front of the house, too. A number that is hard to read from the street, or under 4 inches tall, is an easy fix that avoids a second visit at $40. If the house has a monitored alarm, ask the alarm company for the test report and arrange for someone to be there who can reset the panel.

Finally, ask the Construction Office about permits. A permit left open after a furnace, water heater or deck project is the kind of loose end that can hold up the certificate, and a buyer's attorney may ask about it too.

Interstate 80 clips the northeast corner, reached from Exit 37 on County Route 513, and U.S. Route 46 crosses the south end. NJ Transit trains do not stop in Rockaway, but the Denville and Dover stations are close, on the Morris and Essex and Montclair-Boonton lines. NJ Transit local bus 880 serves the borough, and Lakeland Bus Lines runs Route 46 and Route 80 service along Main Street to Port Authority.

sections.h2: Morris County appeals and estate sales
sections.html:
The Morris County Board of Taxation, at P.O. Box 900, Morristown, holds appeal hearings in person only. Its guidance says an assessment is excessive only if it fails one of two tests: full market value as of the prior October 1 in a revaluation year, or the municipality's common level range in other years. Ask the board for the Rockaway filing date for the tax year you care about.

If you inherited the house, an executor signs the deed and the New Jersey GIT/REP form. A New Jersey estate uses the GIT/REP-3, and an executor who is also a beneficiary signs two forms. The seller owes the state transfer fee at recording, and each band of the rate schedule applies only to the slice of price inside it.

With three offices involved, the order matters more than the speed of any one of them.

  1. Call the Bureau of Fire Prevention first, because its fee is lowest when you book ten or more business days ahead.
  2. Ask the Construction Office whether any permit is still open and finish it.
  3. Request the final water reading with at least 72 hours of notice.
  4. Pay property taxes in full through the closing date.
  5. Hand the certificate, the water reading and the tax receipt to your closing attorney.

A cash buyer who takes the house as it stands can skip repair negotiations, but these three items are still the borough's requirements, and the seller normally handles them.

faqs.q: Who issues the resale certificate in Rockaway Borough?
faqs.a: The Bureau of Fire Prevention. Call 973-625-3473 to schedule, and expect fees from $55 to $200 depending on how close to closing you book.

faqs.q: Does Rockaway require a certificate of continued occupancy for a house sale?
faqs.a: The borough's property maintenance article requires one for nonresidential and mixed buildings, and it exempts residential structures. Ask the Construction Office at 973-627-8035 whether anything else applies to your address.

faqs.q: How do I get a final water reading in Rockaway?
faqs.a: Contact the Water Clerk at 973-627-2000, extension 223. The fee is $60 with at least 72 hours of notice and $95 on shorter notice.

faqs.q: Is Rockaway Borough the same as Rockaway Township?
faqs.a: No. They are separate Morris County municipalities with separate offices, and the borough was split off from the township in 1894. Check your tax bill to see which one you are in.

faqs.q: Who pays the state transfer fee on a Rockaway sale?
faqs.a: The seller owes it at recording, and the amount rises with the price. Your closing attorney can quote the figure.
